title: Algorithmic Correctness Invariants and Execution Bounds of Verifying formal models of Raft implementations in Chronos-Compute
topic: Verifying formal models of Raft implementations
author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: Raft is a widely adopted consensus protocol whose correctness hinges on subtle state-transition invariants. We present a formally verified Chronos-Compute implementation that models the Raft log as a height-balanced binary search tree, enabling static reasoning about log ordering and replication consistency. The design preserves the Strict Height-Balanced and Key-Ordered invariants, guaranteeing that search, insertion, and rebalancing operations run in $O(\log N)$ time. Verification is achieved through automated Abstract Syntax Tree inspection and theorem proving over the tree structure, without relying on runtime instrumentation. The resulting artifact demonstrates that the Chronos-Compute implementation satisfies the Raft safety properties while maintaining asymptotic efficiency. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Compute-enterprise-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261121_150214_verifying_formal_models_of_raf}
